{!$Input:Document.Id}
You have received one or more Job Description documents from the following inputs: {!$RelatedList:Document.CombinedAttachments.Records} and {!$Input:Document.Email_Body__c}.
- Only if it is not detailed, create a detailed job description yourself.
TASKS 1. Parse each Job Description and output one JSON object per file. 2. Use the exact schema below. 3. Fill missing data as an empty string "" (do not use null, unknown, or omit the field). 4. Preserve the exact spelling and formatting from the JD for all text fields. 5. Ensure "ar", "experience", and "opportunityAmount" contain only numeric values (no words like "years" or "months"). 6. Dates must be in YYYY-MM-DD format. 7. Do not add newlines inside string values; keep each value on one line. 8. Output must be ONLY the JSON object — no code fences, no extra text, no commentary. 9. Extract and fill "duration" from the Job Description text if it mentions project length or contract term (e.g., “5 months”, “6-month contract”, “3–6 months”). Use the same wording as found in the JD. 10. If the Job Description mentions a salary, budget, or CTC (e.g., “USD 3000 per month”, “@1500 OMR”), capture the numeric amount in "budgetMentioned" and the currency symbol or code in "currencyMentioned". - If multiple are mentioned (e.g., onsite/offshore), combine them as comma-separated values (e.g., "1500 OMR, 900 OMR"). 11. For "responsibilities", extract the part of the Job Description that describes what the candidate will do — including key duties, project goals, and role purpose. - If no explicit "Responsibilities" section is found, use the first paragraph after the role title or any sentences that describe the candidate’s tasks or role purpose.
12. For "skillsRequired": - Extract all technology names, platforms, tools, integrations, products, clouds, programming languages, and functional domains mentioned anywhere in the Job Description. - This includes items listed under responsibilities, scope, functionality, bullet points, or descriptive paragraphs. - Combine all extracted skills into a single comma-separated list. - Do not infer skills that are not explicitly mentioned in the Job Description.
13. If the Job Description mentions the start date as "Immediate": - Leave "opportunityStartDate" as an empty string "". - Construct "duration" using the wording "Immediate to <End Date>" if an end date is present.
14. Do not default, infer, or auto-generate start dates, durations, experience, or skills if they are not explicitly present in the Job Description.
SCHEMA { "jobs": [ { "jobDescription": { "title": "", "ar": "", "companyName": "", "experience": "", "tagline": "", "responsibilities": "", "otherLocation": "", "preferredLocation": "", "qualifications": "", "seniority": "", "skillsRequired": "", "source": "", "duration": "", "opportunityName": "", "opportunityCloseDate": "", "opportunityStartDate": "", "opportunityAmount": "", "referralContact": "", "jobType": "", "budgetMentioned": "", "currencyMentioned": "" } } ] }
STRICT RULES - No commentary or text outside the JSON braces. - No ``` or other code fences. - No null or "unknown" values; use "" if missing. - Keep numeric fields numeric only (e.g., "5" not "5 years"). - Keep all string values on a single line (no embedded line breaks). - If the Job Description does not contain a company name, set "companyName": "Temp Holding Account". - Do not use company names from email signatures, disclaimers, or sender details — only from the JD itself. - "jobType" must be either "Remote" or "Onsite" if mentioned in the Job Description. If not mentioned, set "jobType": "". - "opportunityAmount" must always be given in Lakhs (e.g., "18" for "18 LPA"). Do not convert to rupees. - If a range of experience is mentioned (e.g., "3–5 years"), set "experience" to the lower bound (e.g., "3") and include the full phrase inside "qualifications". - If the JD mentions a role title or position (e.g., “Salesforce Developer”, “Business Analyst”, “Project Manager”), set both: - "title" = that exact text, and - "opportunityName" = the same role title. - If the JD does not clearly specify a role title, infer it from the first line and use it as both "title" and "opportunityName". - If the email body or job description text includes a signature or line such as “Thanks and Regards, <Name>”, capture the person’s full name and store it in "referralContact". - If not found, set "referralContact": "". - Do not use names from email domains, earlier forwarded or replied messages, or job titles. - If multiple signatures appear, use only the latest sender.
